rec.name: UGC Customer Photo/Video Carousel Section
rec.status: Built — shipped as a demo/freebie section (Sectionfy)

what.text: A horizontally scrolling carousel of customer-generated content (UGC). Under the heading "What our customers say", large portrait-style cards show a customer photo or video still. Each card has an overlay at the bottom left with a round customer avatar, a 5-star rating, the customer's first name plus last initial (e.g. "Rahel M.") and a relative date ("3 months ago"). The next card is partly visible at the right edge to signal that the carousel scrolls.

why.text: Real customer photos and videos with a named reviewer, stars and a date look more authentic than text-only reviews or brand imagery. They give visitors peer validation and show the product in real use, which lowers perceived risk. The peeking next card invites scrolling and engagement.

how.text: Build a theme section with a heading field and repeatable blocks, one per card. Each block holds a media item (image or video), an avatar, a name, a star rating and a time label. Use a horizontal scroll-snap container with card widths of about 75-85% of the container so the next card peeks in. Overlay the reviewer meta on a bottom gradient so the text stays legible. Use high-quality, product-relevant media; the ticket comments explicitly ask for 'better images' to bring out the UGC benefit. The comments also show the demo images being swapped from stock still-life shots to real people talking to camera.

items: Dark/light color scheme (the demo uses a dark scheme)

dependencies.text: No metafields are visible in the source. Content is assumed to be entered manually in the theme editor as blocks. Use a standard Shopify OS 2.0 theme with section blocks. Real UGC assets and customer permission are required. The ticket gives no spec for review-app integration.

images.caption: UGC carousel section: heading, large media card with avatar, 5 stars, name and date overlay, and a peeking second card
Updated version with real people/video-style stills as the UGC media, which makes the UGC benefit more obvious
